items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: I mean, Sidney, we used to take lessons from Piku, same time.

ctx.x: I didn't just went over there, nothing else felt like. Took a little lesson, me and Piku. Another boy that died, uh, Hanukkah, Armageddon, uh, Sidney Veen. That's a classic where he died, too. I mean, Sidney, we used to take lessons from Piku, same time.
What kind of a clarinet player was Piku in those days? Piku was a good clarinet player.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-08-22
items.q: Well, Pequil was a different man. Pequil would play music very suddenly. Yeah, you see, Pequil is a tinsmith.

ctx.x: You were going to say something about Pequil. Was Pequil like that?

Well, Pequil was a different man. Pequil would play music very suddenly. Yeah, you see, Pequil is a tinsmith. He's supposed to be a tinsmith, you understand? And he was laying on with the handle or something. But he was very independent. If he'd come out, it was all right. If he didn't, it was all right. Now, how he'd come out would have spread. But he was such a nice man, he was like that big time. Then again, the little things about Pequil, Pequil was a whole lot jealous of his wife. And that made him make…

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Now you see, I learned from Piku, George.

ctx.x: Later years. But the force would come now. Now you see, I learned from Piku, George. But my ideas were from Lloyd. Now Big R. Louis was a man that played a clarinet. And he could take a clarinet and make a rooster, curl, dog bark, anything like that. And that's why I learned he told him that problem. Right on the end, because if he was playing the hill, I wouldn't dance or go out there. I wouldn't have to hang him or nothing from him.
Would you say he was your favorite of all the ones you heard?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-12-20
items.q: Yeah I went to pico, but all the trouble, if you keep up you'll be a good boy

ctx.x: You know where they learned, who their teacher was or anything?

No I couldn't answer on that. But I know that… That Shara Nees… Oh yeah. You see he was a teacher for most of the musicians. You see? Yeah I've heard a lot about him. Yeah. Now I don't know if he… he… he… he… teach those or not, but he was well known. All the musicians went to him, because I went to him myself. Yeah. Yeah. I went to him myself too. Oh you did. But I didn't keep up, but he tell me, oh that's pico too. I went to pico. Oh yeah, you did. Yeah I went to pico, but all the trouble, if you keep up you'll…
Did George Bakke help people? Did he ever give any regular lessons or help the young fellas?
